live_debug.stats_dsu_clients_tip: Number of active applications (emulators) connected and receiving motion data. If 0, emulator is either not running or not configured for DSU port.
live_debug.stats_hover_hint: Click a card to reveal description
live_debug.stats_in_hz_tip: How many times per second the phone sends data. Usually stays stable (e.g. 60). Sharp drops mean the phone briefly throttled data transmission — typically due to CPU load or screen sleep.
live_debug.stats_jitter_tip: How uneven the packet arrival intervals are over time. A smooth flat line is good. Sawtooth spikes indicate unstable connection, even if average frequency (Hz) looks normal.
live_debug.stats_latency_tip: Transit time from phone to computer. Lower values mean less noticeable delay in game between hand movement and on-screen response. Sharp spikes usually indicate Wi-Fi issues.
live_debug.stats_loss_tip: Count of packets sent by the phone that never reached the computer, calculated by sequence number gaps. Normally 0. Growth indicates signal drops along the route (distance to router, interference, network congestion).
live_debug.stats_modal_desc: Recording stopped (1 min limit reached or stopped manually). Would you like to save the .csv data file to disk?
live_debug.stats_out_gyro_tip: Exact values physically received by the game — final result of all processing steps. If values stick or clip, game controls will feel unresponsive.
live_debug.stats_out_hz_tip: How many times per second data is dispatched to emulator. Should stay close to input frequency — if significantly lower, processing congestion is occurring.
live_debug.stats_pipe_latency_tip: Time spent by the application itself processing one frame — from network arrival to emulator transmission. Latency added purely by our software pipeline.
live_debug.stats_raw_accel_tip: Raw accelerometer readings from phone prior to calibration and gravity filtering.
live_debug.stats_raw_gyro_tip: Raw angular velocity from phone gyroscope exactly as measured, prior to bias subtraction and filtering. Useful for checking hardware sensor noise versus processing issues.

setup.android_desc: No certificate installation needed on Android. Open the controller address directly in Chrome.
setup.android_hint: Tap the chip or scan the QR code above to copy the link.
setup.disclosure_body_1: **What am I installing?** A small security certificate, generated right on your own PC — nothing about it ever leaves your local network. It just tells your phone "trust this one connection" so it can talk to your computer over Wi-Fi. It can't see or touch anything else — not your other apps, not other websites, nothing. The app doesn't send any data anywhere, ever — no analytics, no logs, no phoning home. And since it's all open-source, you don't have to take our word for it: you (or your AI coding assistant) can go read the exact code that generates this certificate right here: [`internal/ca`](https://github.com/MrHoustonOff/iphone-gyro-controller/tree/main/internal/ca).
setup.disclosure_body_2: **Why is this even necessary?** Safari (WebKit) simply refuses to share gyroscope/motion data or keep a live WebSocket connection open unless the page is loaded over a secure, encrypted connection (HTTPS/WSS) — that's an Apple privacy rule, and no app can get around it. Since there's no way to get a "real," publicly-trusted certificate for a private local address, self-signing one and asking your phone to trust it is the only way to satisfy that rule without ever going through the internet.
setup.disclosure_body_3: **The trade-off:** you get a fully private, direct, offline connection where none of your data ever leaves your Wi-Fi — but in exchange, you have to do this one manual "trust" step yourself, since there's no public authority that can vouch for a certificate that only exists on your home network.
setup.disclosure_body_4: No hidden actions. Just transparent local communication for your gamepad.
setup.disclosure_title: Why is this certificate needed and is it safe?
setup.ios_desc: One-time local profile setup for Safari
setup.ios_step1_text: Open the link (or scan the QR code) **on your phone**, then tap `Allow`.
setup.ios_step2_text: Go to `Settings`. A banner reading `Profile Downloaded` will appear at the top of the screen — tap it.
setup.ios_step5_text: Return to the main `Settings` screen. Go to `General` → `About`, then scroll all the way down to `Certificate Trust Settings` and tap it.
setup.ios_step6_text: You'll see your certificate listed. Toggle it on, then tap `Continue`.

settings_modal.subtitle: Server ports, network and motion filtering for advanced users
settings_modal.dsu_port_desc: UDP motion server port for emulators (default: 26760)
settings_modal.dsu_port_tip: UDP port for the Cemuhook DSU motion server. Enter this exact port in your emulator's motion settings (Cemu, RPCS3, Ryujinx, Dolphin, etc.). Default: 26760.
settings_modal.http_port_tip: Local TCP port for smartphone initial pairing and iOS certificate profile download. Default: 8080.
settings_modal.https_port_tip: Secure TLS port for the controller web app. Safari requires HTTPS to access motion sensors. Default: 8443.
settings_modal.filter_live_hint: All filter adjustments apply automatically on the fly. Best tuned directly while aiming inside the game.
settings_modal.gyro_smoothing_tip: Adaptive non-linear 1-Euro filter. Eliminates physiological hand tremor during slow aiming while preserving zero latency on rapid flicks.
settings_modal.gyro_deadband_tip: Smooth Hermite deadband. Completely silences micro-tremors below threshold with no step discontinuities.
settings_modal.gyro_sensitivity_tip: Gyro angular velocity scale factor for emulators (default: 1.00x). Scales aim speed independently of in-game sensitivity sliders.
settings_modal.gyro_deadzone_desc: Suppression of resting electronic sensor noise
settings_modal.gyro_deadzone_tip: Filters micro-noise from the phone gyro when held or resting on a desk, eliminating crosshair drift.
settings_modal.bench_aim_sub: Crosshair tracks real-time filtered DSU angular velocity
settings_modal.bench_platform_sub: 3D shrine apparatus platform tilts with controller motion
settings_modal.bench_sensitivity_note: Test bench response may feel different from gameplay. We **strongly recommend** tuning parameters in our app while testing directly in the game!
settings_modal.bench_fs_hint: Tilt controller • Don't drop the ball! [Esc] Exit
settings_modal.stillness_hint_tip: Show subtle recalibration hint if phone rests motionless on a surface tilted by more than 10 degrees.
settings_modal.disconnect_alert_desc: Red window glow and blur when screen turns off
settings_modal.disconnect_alert_tip: Show warning card with frosted glass blur over calibration dialog if smartphone screen turns off or disconnects.
settings_modal.sound_mode_tip: Play an audio chime when the smartphone connects or suddenly disconnects.
settings_modal.theme_tip: Choose between dark and light appearance modes in GyroBridge.
settings_modal.language_tip: Choose the primary display language for GyroBridge.
settings_modal.btn_reset_tip: Restore all ports and sensor parameters back to factory defaults.

welcome.title: Welcome to GyroBridge!
welcome.p1: With this application, you can use your smartphone (Android or iPhone) as a gyroscope motion source for PC games and emulators!
welcome.p2: This project is completely open source — feel free to review the code or contribute to development!
welcome.step1: 1. Ensure your phone and PC are on the **SAME LOCAL NETWORK**!
welcome.step2: 2. Complete the **initial setup** (needed only once per device).
welcome.step3: 3. After connecting, make sure to **CALIBRATE IT** (one time is enough).
